title: Parent of All, Omnipotent
description: Parent of All, Omnipotent in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 845 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Virtuous Love of Country”, where the book credits them to Aspland's Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Par-ent of all, om-ni-po-tent! In heaven and earth be-low! Through all cre-a-tion's vast ex-tent Whose streams of good-ness flow:

lines: Teach me to know from whence I rose,
No private aims may I propose,
To hear my country's lawful voice
Me from fair freedom's sacred cause
Nor grandeur, gold, nor vain applause,
Let me my public walk pursue:

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
